Lavoisier.summary: ⓐ: in combustion the caloric in gaseous oxygen escapes into the air, and this generates the heat.

c1.text: Combustion is a process in which a substance combines with oxygen.

c3.text: Heat is generated when caloric that had been combined with a substance is released.

c4.text: Gases contain far more caloric than solids or liquids.

c5.text: Gaseous oxygen is a compound of oxygen and caloric.

c6.text: ⓐ In combustion, the oxygen in gaseous oxygen combines with the burning substance, while the caloric in gaseous oxygen escapes into the air, thus generating heat.

h1.text: When many solid substances combust, heat is generated and gas is produced at the same time.

h2.text: Where a solid turns into a gaseous product, the product must take up caloric, so little caloric escapes and ⓐ cannot explain the heat.

a.note: The fact gives no new argument for ⓐ; with c4 it even conflicts with ⓐ, so it does not strengthen.

h3.text: Gunpowder, which contains compounds of oxygen, can combust explosively and release a massive amount of heat even without gaseous oxygen.

h4.text: The heat generated in combustion does not come from caloric escaping from gaseous oxygen.

h5.text: No matter how much heat generated during combustion is released into the air, the mass of the air does not increase.

h6.text: Nothing escapes from gaseous oxygen into the air during combustion.

c.note: Naive inference rc1 (no mass gain, so nothing escaped) is undercut by c2: caloric is massless.
